copy.blurb:
The model fancies Japan more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against Sweden. +14.3pp is a wide disagreement by the engine's standards; that's what fires this as a Pick on the home side.

Public Elo rates Japan 130 points higher than the other side (Japan 1790, Sweden 1660). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Japan to win at 53%, the draw at 22%, and Sweden to win at 25%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. Japan on the win side reads 53%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Japan to win at 38%, the draw at 24%, and Sweden to win at 28%. Polymarket has Japan at 38%, which prices out at American odds of +160; the model has the same side at 53%. The +14.3pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Japan side that lower bound is 43% — +4.3pp clear of the market's 38%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Japan side.

News will move the prior. With kickoff roughly 35 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Japan a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +14.3pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: On every meaningful read, Japan look stronger here than Polymarket has them. Model 53% vs market 38% — a +14.3pp gap on the favourite side.
copy.title: Japan v Sweden · the model leans Japan
